newsitem.title: UK: Dlr/mark firm in Europe but still shy of new highs.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/mark firm in Europe but still shy of new highs.

text.p: The dollar held firm against the mark in morning European trade, hovering around 1.73 after touching a fresh 37-month high overnight at 1.7350 marks.

Expectations of higher U.S. rates, particularly against Germany and Europe, proved the dominating factor for the dollar's strength and the U.S./Germany ten-year yield spread widened to 120 basis points in morning trade.

Appetite for convergence trades in the run up to Europe's monetary union is also on the rise with demand for Europe's EMU hopefuls continuing at the expense of the mark, providing further support for the dollar.
Comments from U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin late Monday that U.S. dollar policy was unchanged and that it would only intervene in forex markets when appropriate caused little surprise.

"The basic thing is there is no policy opposition to the rising dollar, it still has another couple of pfennigs to go before raising (strong dollar) policy risk," said Tony Norfield, treasury economist at ABN-Amro in London.
Dollar/mark stood at 1.7300/05 at 0812 GMT after touching 1.7350 marks overnight but still above late Monday's European level of 1.7258/64 marks.
Market focus was on today's U.S. March consumer price data due at 1230 GMT.
An average of analysts' forecasts point to a monthly rise of 0.2 percent in the headline figure, and 0.3 percent in the core, while a year-on-year rise of 2.9 percent is expected.

"The market is pricing in higher U.S. rates which will only be reinforced by a strong number today," said a German bank dealer. "But a soft number won't do much damage to the dollar given the Fed's pre-emptive monetary policy. This will keep the rate hike talk ticking over for a while."
Mark/yen's decline below key support at 73.00 overnight also helped dollar/mark bulls. The mark extended its fall to 73.85/88 in morning trade from 73.28/32 late Monday.
Dollar/yen slipped back from overnight levels, failing to progress through the mid-126 yen area amid wariness over possible Bank of Japan intervention.

"Few will wish to add to dollar/yen positions directly in the face of intervention risk, especially with the added prospect of Japanese trade figures tomorrow and U.S. (trade) data on Thursday," said Paul Meggyesi, senior currency economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London.
Dollar/yen stood at 126.14/24 against 126.42/47 yen late Monday in Europe.

The mark remained soft against the European high-yielding currencies amid renewed vigour for EMU convergence plays despite a downbeat assessment of EU contries' progress in debt consolidation in today's European Monetary Institute EMI annual report. However, the EMI, the forerunner of European Central Bank, said prospects for sustained low inflation were good.
The Bank of Spain, as expected, trimmed its key money rate to 5.5 percent from 5.75 percent today, underscoring this low inflation outlook, said analysts.

Sterling/mark benefited from dollar/mark strength, pushing to a fresh 4-1/2 year high overnight of 2.8122 marks and holding firm just below this level in morning trade. However, the strong dollar capped the pound against the US currency, posting only a marginal rise to $1.6242/52 from late Monday's $1.6213/23.
